title: embeddings-and-rerank-endpoint-debug-breadcrumbs
content:
Summary:

Quick notes / breadcrumbs while debugging a recurring set of anomalies hitting the embeddings + rerank endpoint over the last 48h. Two things observed repeatedly: (1) intermittent dimension mismatch errors from reranker (client reports 768 vs model 1024) and (2) correlated p99/p95 latency spikes (~2-3x baseline) that coincide with model swap events or fallback paths. This doc is a scratchpad of commands tried, logs, hypotheses, and next steps.

Timeline (high-level):
- 2026-02-26 ~09:30 PST: First pager about elevated p99 on /v1/rerank reported by customer-prod alerts (alert group: rerank-tail-latency-prod).
- 2026-02-26 ~09:45 PST: Observed client-side errors indicating embedding dimension mismatch for some requests (client error: "embedding dim 768 != expected 1024").
- 2026-02-26 ~10:00 PST: Temporary mitigation - route traffic to rerank-v1-stable (older model) for affected orgs. Latency partially recovered.
- 2026-02-27: Additional incidents; sporadic reappearance of mismatch errors even after routing.
- 2026-03-01: Reproduced locally with minimal repro (see repro steps).

Repro steps (start here to reproduce locally):
1) Spawn small local replica of rerank service against the latest embedding model checkpoint (tag: rerank/2026-02-25).
2) Run: curl -s -X POST "https://api-staging.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings:batch" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"embed-small-1024","inputs":["query A","query B"],"return_dim":1024}' | jq .
3) Immediately POST results to rerank endpoint (server expects 1024 dims):
   curl -s -X POST "https://api-staging.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"reranker-v2","candidate_embeddings":<embeddings-json>,"query_embedding":<query-embedding-json>}' | jq .
Notes: Embedding generator has two config paths: the client-side SDK sometimes requests embed-small (default 768 dim) vs embed-small-1024 (explicit). The failing cases trace back to clients that omitted explicit model param and hit a routing logic change introduced 2026-02-24 that made default alias map to embed-small-1024 in some regions.

Commands & checks I ran:
- Check running model versions on staging rerank pods:
  kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=rerank -o wide
  kubectl -n prod exec -it <pod> -- curl localhost:8080/version
  Result: rerank v2 @ commit 1a2b3c4, embedding model alias "embed-default" resolved to embed-small-1024 on us-west, but to embed-small (768) on eu-west due to stale alias cache on routing service.

- Grepped logs for dimension mismatch errors:
  kubectl -n prod logs deploy/rerank --since=6h | egrep -i "dim|dimension|mismatch" -A3 -B2 | sed -n '1,200p'
  Example snippet from logs:
    [2026-02-26T09:42:18Z] ERROR rerank::service - embedding dim mismatch: got=768 expected=1024 src=request-id=abc123 org=org-56 route=us-west
    stacktrace: rerank::ranker::validate_dims at ranker.rs:112

- Looked at routing cache entries on router-service (suspect stale alias map):
  curl -s http://router-svc.internal/aliases/embed-default | jq .
  Returns different mappings across regions; eu-west node had not picked up alias update.

- Measured latency/throughput metrics during spike window (Grafana queries):
  p50: 120ms baseline, p95: 360ms baseline. During spike: p50 140ms, p95 980ms, p99 > 1500ms.
  Correlated with increased CPU on rerank pods and fallback to brute-force scoring (we suspect fallback path executed when embeddings parsing failed).

Error snippets collected:
- Client error (SDK): "Embedding vector has length 768 but reranker expects 1024. Please pass model param or use endpoint /v1/embeddings?model=embed-small-1024"
- Server error (rerank service): "panic: embedding length mismatch; rejecting request (req id abc123)" followed by stack; in other windows, instead of panic, code catches mismatch and runs slow fallback scoring which dramatically increases tail latency.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Alias routing inconsistency: router alias for "embed-default" was updated 2026-02-24 to point to embed-small-1024, but some router instances kept serving the old mapping (embed-small 768). Clients that do not explicitly pass the model param can be routed to either embedding variant depending on region, so we observe mixed dims.
2) SDK default change: A change in SDK (PR #553) introduced an implicit model aliasing when no model param is passed; combined with (1) this produces mixed dims.
3) Model export change: There was a recent export for embed-small-1024 where the model's embedding projection shape changed; combined with a rerank model expecting 1024, mismatch manifests when the two sides are out-of-sync.
4) Rerank service fallback path handling is inefficient: on dimension mismatch we sometimes run a slow fallback (brute-force scoring) instead of rejecting early; that causes latency spikes under load.

Immediate actions taken so far:
- Rolled back router alias to explicit embed-small alias in us-west and eu-west for affected customers (temporary).
- Added stricter validation in rerank service to reject mismatched dims early (PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/nn-reranker/pull/217). This should fail faster and avoid expensive fallback scoring.
- Notified SDK team and posted repro in Slack channel #eng-applied-ml (thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABC123/p1678459200000).

Commands/patches tried (notes):
- Patch to rerank validate_dims: added a short-circuit error that returns 400 to the caller instead of running fallback. Deployed to staging and ran load test. Result: fewer CPU spikes but more client 4xxs (expected) and downstream customers see consistent errors, enabling quick identification.
- Router fix: forced alias refresh on all router instances: kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/router-service ; verified alias consistency with curl to /aliases/embed-default
- SDK change: added explicit model param in our internal clients as a stop-gap.

Outstanding unknowns / follow-ups:
- Why did router instances miss alias update? Investigate router-service config refresh logic and check recent deploys (possible race during 2026-02-24 deploy). Owner: Alex Kim (infra).
- Why do some requests continue to show mismatch after alias fix? Possible client caching of older embedding value or CDN cache. Need sampling of failing request IDs and raw client payloads. Owner: Priya Nair (applied-ml).
- Verify that no older embeddings are persisted in KV caches used by rerank. Check prefix cache TTLs for embeddings-store.

Quick diagnostic queries to run next (placeholders):
- List router instances with last sync time:
  curl router-svc.internal/health | jq .last_alias_sync - for each instance
- Dump a handful of failing request payloads from rerank logs: grep req-id=abc123 -A20 /var/log/rerank/requests.log
- Cross-check SDK version header in failing client requests to map to PR that changed default aliasing.

Longer-term mitigations to propose:
- Stronger request schema validation at the edge (reject mismatched dims at the gateway with clear error) to avoid hit to rerank compute.
- Add dimension metadata to embedding payloads (explicit "dim":1024) and require the reranker to validate before deserializing heavy data.
- Monitoring: new alert when we see >1% of requests with embedding dim != expected for a model alias.
- Rollout policy: when alias update happens, do a coordinated alias refresh with a short TTL and verification across all router instances. Add post-deploy test that queries alias mapping from each router node.

People to loop in / next owners:
- Alex Kim (infra) - investigate router alias sync and rollout.
- Priya Nair (applied-ml) - collect failing request payloads and validate client SDK behavior.
- Taylor Morgan (sre) - confirm alert thresholds and observe if early rejection reduces pager noise.

Misc notes / hunches:
- The dimension mismatch is the immediate trigger for some of the observed latency, but a major contributor to tail is the fallback scoring path. If we either reject faster or ensure consistent embedding dims, tail should normalize.
- I suspect a deploy/rollout race (2026-02-24) where router-service instances that restarted earlier picked up new alias while others remained on old alias. The SDK change that removed explicit model selection made the system fragile to alias drift.

Next steps (short):
- Collect 10 failing request payloads and their full headers + client SDK version.
- Land and promote validate_dims fast-fail to prod after post-review.
- Coordinate with infra to confirm router alias refresh and add automated verification.

If you pick this up: check linked JIRA RWI-4821 for timeline and incident log. I'll keep this doc updated with any new logs or repros.

End of notes.
